fields.Front: In an OOD interview, what are the core functional requirements to clarify for a Traffic Signal Controller system?
fields.Back: 1) Control signal lights at one or more intersections. 2) Support multiple directions (N/S/E/W) with independent light states. 3) Cycle lights in a safe, timed sequence (green→yellow→red). 4) Support emergency-vehicle preemption. 5) Support manual/maintenance override (e.g. flashing red on power failure).

fields.Front: What should you explicitly mark out of scope when designing a Traffic Signal Controller in a 45-minute interview?
fields.Back: Adaptive/ML-based timing optimization, pedestrian-button hardware integration, vehicle-detection sensor hardware, and city-wide synchronization across many intersections — mention them as extensions, don't design them in depth.

fields.Front: What is the responsibility of the SignalController class?
fields.Back: Owns the timing loop: advances the active SignalPhase, tells each TrafficSignal to transition its light, enforces the all-red clearance interval between phases, and exposes hooks for emergency preemption and manual override.

fields.Front: What is the responsibility of the TrafficSignal class, as opposed to SignalController?
fields.Back: It represents the physical light for one direction. It only knows its own current LightColor/state and how to transition to the next one — it has no knowledge of other directions or the overall phase schedule.

fields.Front: What fields does a SignalPhase typically hold?
fields.Back: The set of Directions that are GREEN during this phase, and a durationSeconds for how long the phase lasts before the controller advances to the next phase (optionally, which directions get a protected left-turn arrow).
Composition: an Intersection owns exactly one TrafficSignal per approach direction (e.g. a Map<Direction, TrafficSignal>); the signals cannot exist independently of the intersection.
A SignalController holds an ordered, cyclic list of SignalPhase objects and steps through them one at a time, applying each phase's green directions to the intersection for its configured duration.

fields.Front: Which design pattern best fits the light-color transitions of a single TrafficSignal, and why?
fields.Back: The State pattern. Each color (Red/Yellow/Green) is a state object that knows only its own duration and which state comes next; TrafficSignal.transition() just delegates to currentState.next(). This avoids a large switch/if-else and makes adding a new state (e.g. FlashingRed) a matter of adding one class, without touching existing ones.

fields.Front: Besides State, what secondary pattern helps notify external components (a pedestrian signal, a monitoring dashboard) when a light changes, and why?
fields.Back: Observer. The signal maintains a list of listeners and calls onLightChanged(direction, newColor) on each transition, decoupling the core signal logic from whatever consumes the change event.

fields.Front: What two methods form the minimal public API of the LightState interface in a State-pattern TrafficSignal?
fields.Back: getColor() — returns the LightColor this state represents — and next() — returns the LightState to transition to once this state's duration elapses.

fields.Front: What method does SignalController expose to handle an approaching emergency vehicle, and what must it do internally?
fields.Back: preempt(Direction direction) — pauses the normal phase cycle, forces that direction's signal to GREEN and all conflicting directions to RED, then safely resumes the normal cycle (respecting all-red clearance) once preemption ends.

fields.Front: Why must SignalController insert an all-red clearance interval between phases instead of switching one direction's green directly to another direction's green?
fields.Back: Vehicles already in the intersection from the ending phase need time to clear before cross-traffic gets a green light — without the all-red gap, two conflicting directions could effectively be green/entering at once, causing collisions.

fields.Front: On detecting a power failure or hardware fault, what should SignalController do, and why not simply turn all lights off?
fields.Back: Switch every TrafficSignal into FLASHING_RED mode (each direction treated like a stop sign) rather than going dark — an unlit intersection gives drivers no cue that caution is required, which is far more dangerous than a flashing-red fail-safe.

fields.Front: Edge case: a technician wants to force a specific phase manually from a control panel. How should the design support this without breaking the automatic cycle logic?
fields.Back: Add a manualOverride(SignalPhase phase) entry point that pauses the controller's automatic timer loop (the same pause mechanism used for emergency preemption) and lets the operator hold a phase; resuming exits override mode and re-enters the normal cycle at a safe phase boundary (never mid-phase).

fields.Front: (Java) Implement the LightState interface and its GreenState concrete implementation for the State-pattern TrafficSignal.
fields.Back:
public interface LightState {
    LightColor getColor();
    LightState next();
    int getDurationSeconds();
}

public class GreenState implements LightState {
    @Override
    public LightColor getColor() { return LightColor.GREEN; }

    @Override
    public LightState next() { return new YellowState(); }

    @Override
    public int getDurationSeconds() { return 30; }
}

fields.Front: (Python) Implement TrafficSignal with tick() and transition() driving the State-pattern light changes.
fields.Back:
class TrafficSignal:
    def __init__(self, direction, initial_state):
        self.direction = direction
        self.state = initial_state
        self.elapsed = 0

    def tick(self, seconds=1):
        self.elapsed += seconds
        if self.elapsed >= self.state.get_duration_seconds():
            self.transition()

    def transition(self):
        self.state = self.state.next()
        self.elapsed = 0

    def color(self):
        return self.state.get_color()

fields.Front: (Java) Implement SignalController.tick(), called once per second, driving the phase cycle with an all-red clearance interval between phases.
fields.Back:
public class SignalController {
    private static final int ALL_RED_SECONDS = 2;
    private List<SignalPhase> phases;
    private int currentPhaseIndex = 0;
    private int elapsedInPhase = 0;
    private boolean inAllRedClearance = false;

    public void tick() {
        elapsedInPhase++;
        SignalPhase phase = phases.get(currentPhaseIndex);

        if (inAllRedClearance) {
            if (elapsedInPhase >= ALL_RED_SECONDS) {
                advanceToNextPhase();
            }
            return;
        }

        if (elapsedInPhase >= phase.getDurationSeconds()) {
            setAllDirectionsRed();
            inAllRedClearance = true;
            elapsedInPhase = 0;
        }
    }

    private void advanceToNextPhase() {
        currentPhaseIndex = (currentPhaseIndex + 1) % phases.size();
        inAllRedClearance = false;
        elapsedInPhase = 0;
        applyPhase(phases.get(currentPhaseIndex));
    }
}

fields.Front: (Java) Implement SignalController.preempt() for emergency-vehicle handling, saving state so the normal cycle can resume afterward.
fields.Back:
public class SignalController {
    private SignalPhase savedPhase;
    private int savedElapsed;
    private boolean preempted = false;

    public void preempt(Direction emergencyDirection) {
        savedPhase = phases.get(currentPhaseIndex);
        savedElapsed = elapsedInPhase;
        preempted = true;

        setAllDirectionsRed();
        getSignal(emergencyDirection).forceColor(LightColor.GREEN);
    }

    public void resumeFromPreemption() {
        setAllDirectionsRed();      // all-red clearance first
        preempted = false;
        applyPhase(savedPhase);
        elapsedInPhase = savedElapsed;
    }
}

fields.Text: The core classes in a Traffic Signal Controller design are {{c1::Intersection}} (owns the signals for a junction), {{c2::TrafficSignal}} (one per direction, holds current light state), {{c3::SignalController}} (drives the timing/phase cycle), and {{c4::SignalPhase}} (defines which directions are green together and for how long).
The LightColor enum for a traffic signal is typically {{c1::RED}}, {{c2::YELLOW}}, {{c3::GREEN}}, plus a fail-safe value {{c4::FLASHING_RED}} used during power failure or maintenance.
